full_judgment: 3. The appellant as defendant No.1 contested the said suit by filing written statement, contending, inter alia, the land of plots No.617 and 619 was Khas land of the government. The total land of plot No.617 is 38 decimals while the total land of plot No.619 is 208 decimals. The predecessor of the plaintiffs Mukunda Lal Das was given settlement of 12 decimals land of plot No.617 situated on the south side of the plot and 13 decimal lands of plot No.619 situated on the north side of the plot by Nothi No.78(XIII). The rest land measuring 26 decimals of plot No.617 was vacant. The defendant No.1 acquired 12 decimal lands of plots No.1542 and 1543 adjacent to plot No.617. The defendant No.1 was in possession of 12 decimals land on the northern side of plot No.617. When the defendant No.1 was in possession of the said 12 decimals land, plaintiffs' father applied to re-fix the areas of 25 decimals settled land and Miscellaneous Case No.8(XIII) was started in the office of the defendant No.3 and by order dated 5-5-1966 it was found that the land possessed by the defendant No.1 is not settled land of plaintiffs' father. Thereafter, in pursuance to direction by the authority a team headed by Magistrate Zahedul Islam after due enquiry submitted report and as per report it was found that the defendant No.1 did not possess the settled land of plaintiffs. The defendant No.1 did not claim the land of plot No.619 and did not threaten the plaintiffs to dispossess, hence the suit is liable to be dismissed.
